corrects: PR #6564 (merged 56c47a0782) and PR #6424, in opposite directions
question: does the N=4/N=5 signature survive, and which c_5 does AGENTS.md's size-mismatch figure use?
answer: AGENTS.md's 0.577 ppb uses the SUPERSEDED c_5; under the live c_5 the first omitted term is 0.0561 ppb against a measured 0.055, so the size mismatch evaporates. The signature itself SURVIVES on magnitude under the live family and does not under the superseded one.
scope: (a); c_3 hardcoded at the proton extraction, proton pin only

assertions.name: agents_md_omitted_term_used_the_superseded_c5
assertions.detail: AGENTS.md's 0.577 ppb tracks the SUPERSEDED c_5 (|c_5 u^5| = 0.614697), not the live one (0.0561488); the figure is off by 10.95x

assertions.name: size_mismatch_evaporates_under_the_live_c5
assertions.detail: with the live c_5 the first omitted term is 0.0561488 ppb against a measured 0.055 ppb -- 2 % apart, exactly what an EXACT series predicts. The 'anomalously good landing, ~10x smaller' is an artifact of the superseded coefficient and points the other way.

assertions.name: nonmonotonicity_holds_under_LIVE_and_not_under_superseded
assertions.detail: |residual| goes 6.16983 -> 6.22597 ppb under the LIVE c_5 (increases, so the signature holds) and 6.16983 -> 5.55513 under the superseded one (decreases) -- the OPPOSITE of what my PR #6424 concluded, which read the SIGNED column

assertions.name: crossing_margin_is_small_and_is_reported_as_such
assertions.detail: the N=4 -> N=5 magnitude crossing under the live family is only 0.9101 %, computed with a hardcoded c_3 at one pin; a full settlement re-extracts c_3 at both pins. This probe establishes the direction and the coefficient question, not a final margin.
